quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be careful. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane that belongs to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane that belongs to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must cross the centerline and use the oncoming traffic lane. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is affected by all of the following except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Being physically fit does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic control signs, the vehicle coming from the right has the right-of-way. You must yield to them.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead and pull in front of the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give cyclists plenty of space. Cyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly or too close can push them off-course.

questions.question: When may you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. The only time you may cross a solid yellow line is when you are turning.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before it turns red.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, you may continue through.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a steady green traffic light?

options.text: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed. However, watch for pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. Be ready to slow down if the light changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you are not allowed to park in this area.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use your parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is approaching or ahead of you. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the green arrow is with a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. You must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Big vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that you cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles with lights or sirens go first. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Check that only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Check that only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Check that only children have buckled their seat belts.
Check that all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt before starting the car. Make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the nearest rail when warning signals are flashing. Watch for lowered gates or sounds of an oncoming train.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You may cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes as long as it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction you must drive. It means traffic flows in only one direction on this street.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, when there is bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main traveled portion.
Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
Turn on your high beam headlights to make sure the other vehicle sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main traveled portion.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles traveling toward you at least half of the main traveled portion of the road. Both drivers need enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Under no conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn and flashing red or blue lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle starts to straighten out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to the direction you came from. This is the lane nearest your previous lane.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Look through your back window for pedestrians and obstacles. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially when children are nearby. Get out of the vehicle and check behind it before backing into or out of a driveway.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road if an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams. This keeps you from being blinded and allows you to see well enough to stay on your course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when approaching a school bus that is displaying flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic moving in both directions must stop and remain stopped as long as the red lights are flashing and/or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: You hear a siren while driving, but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down. Do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but cannot tell where the emergency vehicle is, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Try to get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Passing another vehicle increases the chance of a collision. If you drive faster than the traffic around you, you will need to pass many vehicles. Drive with traffic flow, at the legal speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing.
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What helps prevent fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On a long trip, stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely to nap or find a place to stay overnight.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. This is worse in hot weather, when heat causes more oil to rise to the surface.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver must be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create powerful wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles at high speeds.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger directs you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are active.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: The driver
Child passengers
Adult passengers
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: In Nevada, everyone in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Children under six years old or under 60 pounds must use an approved child restraint system.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: On an incline.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space reduces the chance of a collision.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 and older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curve ahead.
Roadwork ahead.
Merging traffic.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for road hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of an upcoming curve.

questions.question: Highway signs that alert drivers to hazards are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. Obey them for your safety. Ignoring warning signs can cause accidents.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: Which recommendation does not help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Be aware that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights shrinks your pupils. When the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the dark. During this time, you cannot see clearly.

questions.question: When can you drive in a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?

options.text: You are driving faster than the flow of traffic.
You are driving more slowly than the flow of traffic.
Your vehicle has multiple occupants.
You are in a hurry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has multiple occupants.
questions.explanation: Some highways reserve the left lane for vehicles with multiple passengers. These HOV lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the pavement.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once moving onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use high beam headlights to see better.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.
